    Display levels from positive and negative reference cells

    Source: R/image-windows.R
    sg_display_levels.Rd

    Sets the black and full-colour levels of each channel from the signal around reference cells, so that called-negative cells stay dark and called-positive cells reach full colour: for every channel up to n negative and n positive cells are drawn, a statistic of the (2 * half + 1)-pixel square patch around each cell is taken ("mean" or a percentile given as a probability), and the levels are the black quantile of the negative and the white quantile of the positive cell values.

    Usage

    sg_display_levels(
  path,
  channels,
  cells,
  positive,
  negative,
  x = "x",
  y = "y",
  label = "label",
  pixel_size = 1,
  half = 7,
  statistic = 0.9,
  black = 0.5,
  white = 0.5,
  n = 300,
  seed = 0
)

    Arguments

    path

    Path to the image file.

    channels

    Channel names.

    cells

    Data frame of cells with positions and labels.

    positive, negative

    Named lists: channel name to the labels of the positive and negative reference cells.

    x, y, label

    Column names in cells (positions in physical units).

    pixel_size

    Physical size of one pixel.

    half

    Patch half-width in pixels.

    statistic

    "mean" or a probability for a patch percentile.

    black, white

    Quantiles across negative and positive cells.

    n

    Maximum number of reference cells per set.

    seed

    Random seed for the draws (the global RNG state is restored).

    Value

    A data frame with columns channel, lo, hi, n_negative and n_positive.

    Details

    Arguments that vary by channel (half, statistic, black, white) accept a single value or a named list/vector by channel name, with an optional .default entry.

    See also

    sg_slide_display_ranges(), sg_display_range()

    Examples

    f <- tempfile(fileext = ".tif")
plane <- matrix(10, 40, 40)
plane[21:40, ] <- 200
invisible(tiff::writeTIFF(plane / 255, f, bits.per.sample = 8L))
cells <- data.frame(x = c(5, 15, 25, 35), y = c(5, 10, 30, 35),
                    label = c("neg", "neg", "pos", "pos"))
sg_display_levels(f, "ch1", cells, positive = list(ch1 = "pos"),
                  negative = list(ch1 = "neg"), half = 2)
#>   channel lo  hi n_negative n_positive
#> 1     ch1 10 200          2          2
